title: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer
tagline: Every choice you make builds your future self.
credits: Story state machine for the web player. Code and text written with AI assistance (Claude Fable 5.2); idea and direction by Faris.

weather.name: Space-weather scientist
weather.does: You read the Sun and warn the crew before a storm.

power.name: Power engineer
power.does: You keep the base's electricity running.

doctor.name: Space doctor
doctor.does: You keep the crew healthy and track their radiation.

farmer.name: Space farmer
farmer.does: You grow the food, and the plants make the air.

comms.name: Comms engineer
comms.does: You keep the base talking to Earth and to its robots.

1.name: Chapter 1
1.title: Who will you become?
1.goal: Make 3 choices. They decide your job on the Moon.

options.label: The engines
options.about: The fire and the noise that lift a rocket

options.label: The Sun satellite
options.about: A small satellite that measures the Sun's storms

options.label: The crew
options.about: The four people riding on top

options.label: Solar racer
options.about: A car that runs on sunlight

options.label: Send a signal
options.about: Say hello to a satellite by radio

choice.prompt: Pick a door. This is who you become.

options.label: Bury the shelter
options.about: Pile Moon dirt on the roof. Dirt blocks radiation.
options.why: Moon dirt on the roof blocks radiation. The rover drained the battery.

options.label: Charge the batteries
options.about: Turn the solar panels to the Sun before it gets rough.
options.why: Full batteries for the long wait. The roof stayed thin.

options.label: Call it early
options.about: Your sensor saw the first particles. Start both jobs now.
options.why: You read the first particles and started sooner. Time for both jobs, but nobody checked the air system.

choice.prompt: The battery is dropping. Greenhouse lights?

options.label: Lights on
options.about: The lettuce keeps making oxygen. The lights eat power.
options.why: The plants kept making oxygen. The lights ate power.

options.label: Lights off
options.about: Save power. Without light, the lettuce stops making oxygen.
options.why: Power saved. The lettuce wilted and stopped making oxygen: it takes 3 to 4 weeks to grow back.

options.label: Use the night battery
options.about: Run the lights from the spare battery. It will be empty later.
options.why: Lights and air both ran. The spare battery was meant for the two-week lunar night.

options.label: Carry the trays in
options.about: Bring the lettuce into the shelter. One more trip through thin walls.
options.why: The plants cleaned the air where you breathe. The trip went through the thin-walled room.

options.label: Stay put
options.about: Stay behind the thick wall. The air cleaner stays frozen.
options.why: Safe behind the thick wall. Nobody reset the air cleaner, so the air went stale.

options.label: Dash out
options.about: Run to the switch. You take radiation at the storm's peak.
options.why: Fresh air. You took radiation at the worst moment of the storm.

options.label: Lowest badge goes
options.about: Send whoever has taken the least radiation, for the shortest trip.
options.why: You sent the person with the lowest dose badge, for the shortest time.

options.label: Reset it by remote
options.about: Drive the rover to the switch from inside. It uses the battery.
options.why: You drove the rover from inside. Nobody took a dose. The rover drained the battery.

you.text: This astronaut is you, all grown up.

goal.text: Your choices decide which space job you get.

launch.title: Launch night, April 2026
launch.text: A Saudi satellite called SHAMS flew toward the Moon with the Artemis II crew, to measure radiation from the Sun.

choose.text: Tap a choice on the screen. Each one opens doors to space jobs.

madak.title: A real competition
madak.text: The Madak space competition (2024) was open to ages 6 to 18. Ten winning experiments flew to the International Space Station.

academy.text: Each door is a job on the Moon base. Your choices opened these doors.

pipeline.title: The real path
pipeline.text: Two Saudi astronauts flew to the International Space Station in May 2023. The SARI 2 programme helps university students build and launch small satellites.

mission.text: Your mission: keep the Moon base alive through a storm from the Sun.

place.title: Malapert Massif
place.text: A mountain near the Moon's south pole. NASA named it as one of the places astronauts may land.

meters.text: Power runs the machines. Air is what you breathe. Shield blocks radiation.

rule.text: Keep all three above zero. Your lowest one decides the ending.

flare.title: Solar flare
flare.text: A giant explosion on the Sun. Its light reaches us in 8 minutes. The harmful particles come later.

radiation.title: Radiation
radiation.text: Tiny, very fast particles from the Sun. They pass through thin walls and can harm people and computers.

shelter.text: The storm shelter has the thickest walls. The crew waits here.

radlab.title: Why shielding matters
radlab.text: In a real storm in September 2017, a detector inside the Space Station read about 1.5 times its normal dose. A thinly shielded one in lunar orbit read more than 1,000 times.

bitflip.title: Bit flip
bitflip.text: A particle can hit a computer chip and flip a 1 into a 0. The computer then does the wrong thing until it is reset.

delay.title: Deciding alone
delay.text: A radio message crosses from the Moon to Earth in 1.3 seconds. From Mars it can take up to 22 minutes, so crews must be ready to decide alone.

learn_engines.title: Rocket engines
learn_engines.text: An engine throws hot gas out the back, very fast. That pushes the rocket the other way: up.

learn_sun.title: Watching the Sun
learn_sun.text: The Sun sometimes throws out bursts of radiation. Satellites like SHAMS measure them, so crews can be warned.

learn_crew.title: Around the Moon
learn_crew.text: In April 2026 a crew of four flew around the Moon. The last people to travel that far went in 1972.

learn_seeds.title: Space gardens
learn_seeds.text: Plants can grow in space. On the Space Station, NASA grew tomatoes for 101 days.

learn_racer.title: Solar power
learn_racer.text: A solar panel turns sunlight into electricity. No light, no power: that is why a shadow stops a solar car.

learn_radio.title: Radio
learn_radio.text: A radio signal travels at the speed of light. From the Moon to Earth it takes 1.3 seconds.

storm._note: One real storm is drawn each run from web/data/donki.json (pulled from NASA's DONKI API). The rule below is the only game rule that depends on it. Archived data: never shown as live.
storm.taxWhy: The storm arrived before the work was finished
storm.waivedWhy: You called it early: no shield lost

endings.rule: Your lowest meter decides the ending.

thrive.name: The outpost thrives
thrive.title: The outpost rode out the storm.
thrive.line: Nothing ran empty. Back to work.

lesson.name: Safe, with a lesson
lesson.title: Everyone is safe. One thing ran low.
lesson.line: Now you know why that meter matters.

evac.name: Home early, safe
evac.title: Home early, and safe.
evac.line: One meter hit empty, so the crew flew home. The next crew will use your notes.

common: Space competitions for school students, like Madak (2024), whose winning experiments flew to the Space Station.
SARI 2: build and launch a small satellite as a student team.
Saudi astronauts have already flown: two went to the Space Station in May 2023.

weather.real: SHAMS, a Saudi satellite, flew with the Artemis II crew in 2026 to measure radiation from the Sun.

power.real: A night on most of the Moon lasts about two weeks, and the surface drops below minus 170 degrees Celsius. Power is everything.

doctor.real: On long missions astronauts lose about 1 to 1.5 percent of their bone density each month. Space doctors fight that.

farmer.real: NASA grew tomatoes on the Space Station for 101 days. Lettuce takes 21 to 28 days.

comms.real: A signal from the Moon reaches Earth in 1.3 seconds. From Mars it can take 22 minutes.
